title: Ask the question that creates the product
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would make this smaller, faster or easier?

Jose described an inventor who asked: there are devices that are this big and use tapes; is it possible to make it smaller, lighter and beautiful, something you carry in your pocket? He said the question created a market.
He said that in the old days the news was on from six to seven, and a viewer who missed it had to wait until the next day, so someone saw a need to watch it any time.
A student gave an example of a Sunday drive that led to one decision, to turn up a driveway, and the consequences were large.
Jose said there were massive consequences to that one decision, and that the black swan is just a name; the main thing is to be aware of it.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the thing your customers find too big or too slow.
Write the question: is it possible to make it smaller.
Write the time they cannot use your service.
Write the one decision you made on a feeling.
Write the next question you will ask.

check.q: What question did the inventor ask?
choices: Is it possible to make it smaller
Is it possible to sell it

check.q: What did Jose say a black swan is?

recap: Ask the question that makes it smaller. Notice one decision's reach.
